Task Name: 4.1 Diagnose the mobile pairing persistence defect
Notes: Diagnosis: not a narrow pairing bug. An earlier merge (3e7f217) silently deleted the ENTIRE app/src/main/ Android source tree plus gradlew/build.gradle.kts/settings.gradle.kts/gradle.properties/gradle-wrapper.properties (git 3-way merge applied an unflagged deletion since main had already dropped the app and mobile had not touched those files since the fork point). Module could not compile. Fixed: all 35 files restored from mobile's pre-merge tip (commit f84c535). Also found and fixed a second, separate bug while getting the full JVM suite to actually run: EventsViewModelTest/HomeViewModelTest hung forever in runTest{} cleanup because their ViewModels' perpetual polling loops (viewModelScope, delay-based) were never cancelled; fixed with vm.viewModelScope.cancel() after each test's assertions. Full JVM suite now runs in ~15s: 37/38 passing (1 pre-existing, documented DataStore-dispatcher-vs-virtual-clock limitation, not a production bug).

Task Name: 4.2 Fix pairing persistence and prove it with an instrumented test
Notes: Proven with a real instrumented test, not the flaky JVM one: app/src/androidTest/.../TokenStorePersistenceTest.kt (4 tests) writes a server URL and token through one TokenStore instance, then reads them back through brand-new TokenStore instances against the same on-device DataStore file and real Android Keystore, the direct on-device equivalent of an app restart or update. Fixed one bug in it before it could run (a @Before method's expression body returned TokenStore instead of Unit, which JUnit4 rejects). Ran on a freshly created android-35 google_apis x86_64 emulator (svcs_test AVD): all 4 pass, 0 failures. This is the deterministic proof the ServerSettingsViewModelTest JVM test structurally cannot give (see 4.1 note).
